claim.why_it_matters: The PDF prints the Arguments-column and Type-column code legends as one entry per line; the markdown writes them as consecutive lines with no list markup or line breaks, so rendered Markdown joins each legend into one run-on line ('A means alphabetic I means integer N means numeric X means alphanumeric'). The text survives in the source but the printed list structure is lost when rendered.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page A-29 (PDF p859) shows both legends (Arguments: A/I/N/X; Type: I/N/X) one entry per line. page-859.md lines 33-36 and 40-42 carry exactly the same entries, one per line, in the same order with the same wording; the claim's own pdf_says and markdown_says are identical. Nothing is missing, misplaced or changed in content; the only point raised is how a Markdown renderer would join soft line breaks, which is formatting, not a content discrepancy.
